    counted:: boolean: false
    // How it takes its height: fill, fit, or share.
    height:: string: fill
    // Whether its contents scroll within it.
    scrolls:: boolean: true

        ${self.counted ? "At its header's right, how many rows it lists, in smaller text, muted." : "It shows no count of what it lists."}

    description:

        file icon, then its file name alone, without its folders, cut off with
        an ellipsis when the sidebar is too narrow, its full path in its

# Referenced Files Panel

## Concept

### Pitch

The top panel of the [ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](ReferencedSpecSidebarScope.md): the spec files the running task references.

### Shape

#### Description

One row per spec file the running task references, each listed once: first those its prompt imports from, then the rest in the order they are first referenced. Each row shows its file icon, then its file name alone, without its folders, cut off with an ellipsis when the sidebar is too narrow, its full path in its tooltip. A file named index, whatever its extension, such as `index.pi`, shows the folder it is in before its name, as `chat-input/index.pi`, and no folder above that.

#### Referencing

A spec file is one in the spec location, as the [ProjectLocationsScope](../../../scope/project-locations/ProjectLocationsScope.md) says; a compiled spec file is one under `.claude/reference`, which stands for part of the spec. Both are listed, and files anywhere else are not. A file's full path counts however long it is, and a relative path is read from the project directory.
A file is referenced, however the harness reads it, when:

- the task's prompt imports from it, its hidden anchor naming it
- the harness reads, edits, or writes it with a file tool
- a shell command reads it, such as cat, head, tail, sed, less, grep, rg, awk, or diff naming it, or a pattern or folder that takes it in, as far as the command shows
- a shell command edits or writes it, such as sed -i, a redirect (> or >>), tee, mv, or cp onto it
- a search tool, Grep or Glob, searches a folder or pattern that takes it in and its results name it
- a subagent the harness starts does any of the above

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

# Table Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

A table of rows under a header of named columns, that can grow long and keep growing while it is shown, and stays smooth however long it gets.

### Shape

- description: A header row naming each column, above one row per item, in order. Every table is a table, as its own scope says: it names its columns, whether it has the lock to the bottom, and what rows it can collapse, and those decide how it is drawn. Each use says what each row holds and where it sits.
  legibility: The table should be readable at a glance. Make sure the font size is large enough, and that the colours are legible in both light and dark mode.
- description: The header row names each column, and stays at the top of the table while the rows scroll beneath it. It has the bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md), lifting it slightly off the rows beneath.
- description: The rows scroll beneath the table's header with a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/ScrollbarScope.md), with or without its lock to the bottom. Locked, the table follows its latest rows. Unlocked, it still follows new rows while it is already scrolled to the bottom, and stays put once scrolled away from it.
- description: However many rows the table grows to, drawing it costs no more than drawing the rows in view, so scrolling, animations, and new rows stay smooth. This holds wherever the table is used: every use shows it the same way, with only the rows in view laid out. While the end of the table is scrolled out of view, a change that would only touch rows out of view redraws nothing.
Drawing a row takes the same little work whichever row it is and however many rows there are. Only rows that are new, or whose content changed, are laid out again; what a row shows that never changes once known is worked out once.
- description: The rows out of view are measured a few at a time over the frames after they arrive, so the scrollbar comes to know the table's full height without any one frame laying out every row. Until a row has been measured, it counts as tall as it last was, or as the rows measured so far on average.
  resizing: When the table's width changes, only the rows in view are laid out anew straight away, staying where they are, and the rest are measured again the same way.
  steadiness: Once measured, the scrollbar's thumb holds still: it never jumps as rows come into view while scrolling, and rows added below while scrolled away from the end leave it where it is.
- description: A table that can collapse a run of rows at its start, and whose use says it does, shows in their place a first row reading "Show 1 …" or "Show N …", naming them, muted, beside a right chevron, with the rest of the rows beneath it.
  toggling: A single click on that row expands them in place, above the rest, and the row then reads "Hide 1 …" or "Hide N …" beside a down chevron; clicking it again collapses them. Each table is expanded or collapsed on its own.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

##### Description

The header row names each column, and stays at the top of the table while the rows scroll beneath it. It has the bevel of the [ThemeScope](../../theme/ThemeScope.md), lifting it slightly off the rows beneath.

#### Scrolling

##### Description

The rows scroll beneath the table's header with a [ScrollbarScope](../scrollbar/ScrollbarScope.md), with or without its lock to the bottom. Locked, the table follows its latest rows. Unlocked, it still follows new rows while it is already scrolled to the bottom, and stays put once scrolled away from it.

#### Drawing

##### Description

However many rows the table grows to, drawing it costs no more than drawing the rows in view, so scrolling, animations, and new rows stay smooth. This holds wherever the table is used: every use shows it the same way, with only the rows in view laid out. While the end of the table is scrolled out of view, a change that would only touch rows out of view redraws nothing.
Drawing a row takes the same little work whichever row it is and however many rows there are. Only rows that are new, or whose content changed, are laid out again; what a row shows that never changes once known is worked out once.

#### Measuring

##### Description

The rows out of view are measured a few at a time over the frames after they arrive, so the scrollbar comes to know the table's full height without any one frame laying out every row. Until a row has been measured, it counts as tall as it last was, or as the rows measured so far on average.

##### Resizing

When the table's width changes, only the rows in view are laid out anew straight away, staying where they are, and the rest are measured again the same way.

##### Steadiness

Once measured, the scrollbar's thumb holds still: it never jumps as rows come into view while scrolling, and rows added below while scrolled away from the end leave it where it is.

#### Collapsed Rows

##### Description

A table that can collapse a run of rows at its start, and whose use says it does, shows in their place a first row reading "Show 1 …" or "Show N …", naming them, muted, beside a right chevron, with the rest of the rows beneath it.

##### Toggling

A single click on that row expands them in place, above the rest, and the row then reads "Hide 1 …" or "Hide N …" beside a down chevron; clicking it again collapses them. Each table is expanded or collapsed on its own.

#### Legibility

The table should be readable at a glance. Make sure the font size is large enough, and that the colours are legible in both light and dark mode.

I've split the table component into sub-files in `spec/ui/components/table/`, following the pattern the sidebar uses with `Sidebar.pi` and `Panel.pi`. `piton build` passes, and I didn't touch anything in `src/`.

| File | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `Table.pi` | An abstract anchor `Table`, registered as the keyword `table`. Its three properties (`columns`, `lock`, `collapses`) set what its `table` section says. |
| `Header.pi` | `TableHeaderShape`: the header stays at the top and has the theme's bevel |
| `Scrolling.pi` | `TableScrollingShape`: the `ScrollbarScope`, and how the table follows new rows when locked or unlocked |
| `Drawing.pi` | `TableDrawingShape`: only the rows in view are laid out, and only new or changed rows are laid out again |
| `Measuring.pi` | `TableMeasuringShape`: rows out of view are measured a few at a time, including after a width change, so the thumb never jumps |
| `CollapsedRows.pi` | `TableCollapsedRowsShape`: the "Show N …" / "Hide N …" row and how clicking it toggles |
| `index.pi` | `TableScope`, with each shape above placed under a named section of `TableShape`, plus a legibility section |

**`Table` properties:**
- **`columns`** is what the header reads.
- **`lock`** is `on` or `off` (which one it starts as), `none` for no lock, or `each use` (the default) when every use of the table says.
- **`collapses`** is what the collapsible rows are called, or null if the table never collapses any.

`TaskTableScope` is now written with the `table` keyword, with `columns: Type, Output, and Status` and `collapses: step`. Its reference page now reads "Show 1 step" / "Show N steps" from that property, so I took that wording out of its own collapsed-steps section. Everything else specific to a harness run is unchanged: types, status, replies, tool calls, streaming, and the scrolling details about the waiting row.

I first tried giving the concept a list of shapes. That rendered each shape as an unlabelled bullet with no heading, so I nested each one under its own named section instead. In the generated `TableScope.md` they now show as Header, Scrolling, Drawing, Measuring and Collapsed Rows headings.
